explain_task.question: Using the revised model only, explain why the LP relaxation can report a feasible objective 32.747162426614494 while the MIP solve is infeasible, and identify one binding/active mechanism from the relaxation and one hard integrality-driven conflict from the integer model. Your answer must trace the exact start variable family `x[(b,v,t)]` and active indicator family `y[(v,t)]` back to the business terms and the CSV inputs, explicitly naming the columns `Vat_2_Time`, `planning_horizon_T`, `peak_energy_cap`, `peak_energy_multiplier`, and the rounded processing times for at least batches 2 and 3 on Vat 2. Also interpret the business meaning of the shadow price of the peak-energy-cap constraint (or, if its dual value is unavailable in the integer solve, the LP-relaxation marginal meaning), state what zero slack would mean, and explain why that marginal value cannot be linearly extrapolated to large policy changes such as relaxing the Vat 2 outage or changing the cap by several units; finally, compare to the original model and pinpoint the exact code/model additions that caused the objective to move from 14.1 to 34.75.
